conviction_note: Findings sum to +1.9 on a beat-and-raise pattern (Q2 revenue $182.2m vs $179.5m guide top, FY raised $11m) and a low H2 billings bar (7-8% guided vs 16% in Q2), against a +7.62 put skew, a +7% intraday run into the print and a stock above most published targets; abs move set at 10 (option-implied 9.91, last four prints 13.8/1.4/13.3/20.6) and p_up 55 rather than 57 because the lean runs against the skew, giving (2*0.55-1)*10 = +1.0, about half the findings' sum.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $185.5-187.5m (8-K ex99.1, 2026-08-04, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001107843/000110784326000034/qlys-20260804xex991.htm) and Benzinga consensus $186.6m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/QLYS/earnings-forecasts) agree at ~$186.5-186.6m. Non-GAAP EPS guide $1.91-1.98; the EPS consensus is NOT resolved (Benzinga shows $1.86, below the guide; Earnings Whispers shows $1.46, likely GAAP), so EPS-dependent sizing is capped. Billings bar: management guided H2 current calculated billings growth to 7-8% (secondary call summary only, https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3669092/qlys-q2-deep-dive-ai-powered-risk-operations-drive-growth-and-strategic-shifts), against a Q3 2025 comp of $186.4m CCB (+11.4%), implying roughly $199-201m.
positioning_check: Short interest 3.23m shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, 5.0 days to cover, on 34.6m shares outstanding = ~9.3% of shares out (https://massive.com/quote/qlys, read 2026-11-09); 3.28m / 4.9 days at 2026-09-30. Baseline skew +7.62 vol points (25d put over call), put/call OI 1.19, priced lean 'downside paid'; event-implied move 9.91%, straddle 13.36% to 2026-11-20. Stock traded $224.95 on 2026-10-26, ~$230 52-week high late Oct, closed $190.41 on 2026-11-06, and was +7.2% at $204.12 intraday 2026-11-09 (spot sealed $201.70). Moderately crowded short, not extreme; the skew is the market's stated downside lean.

findings.finding: Qualys has beaten the top of its own revenue guide and raised the FY range at each of the last two prints: Q1 2026 $175.6m and FY raised from $717-725m to $721-727m; Q2 2026 $182.2m against a $177.5-179.5m guide ($2.7m, 1.5% over the top) and FY raised by $11m to $732-738m. The FY midpoint implies Q4 2026 revenue of only ~$190.7m (~+8.5% y/y against 11% in Q2), so the same pattern points to Q3 revenue near $188-189m against the ~$186.6m bar and another FY raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise was bought hard: Q2 2026 (2026-08-04) +13.78%, Q3 2025 (2025-11-04) +20.56%. Q1 2026 beat-and-raise went -1.41%; Q4 2025 fell -13.31% on a weak first FY guide (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: The beat-and-raise habit is widely known (7 of 8 EPS beats per Earnings Whispers), so part of it is in the price; what is not visible is the size: consensus sits at the guide midpoint ($186.6m) instead of above the guide top as it would if the street were modelling a Q2-sized beat, and the implied Q4 deceleration to ~8.5% is still in the FY range.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 8-K shows the same pattern a quarter earlier (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001107843/000110784326000013/qlys-20260505xex991.htm). Same company, so not an independent counterparty.

findings.finding: Management guided second-half current calculated billings growth to only 7-8% after Q2 CCB of $176.5m grew 16% (against an 8% comp in Q2 2025); the Q3 2025 comp is $186.4m (+11.4%), so the guide implies Q3 2026 CCB of roughly $199-201m. Billings is the line this stock's reactions have turned on, and that bar is low relative to the most recent quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 CCB +16% (from +8% in Q1) coincided with the +13.78% reaction; Q1 2026 CCB +8% with -1.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: The 7-8% H2 billings guide appears only in call summaries, not in the release table; if the market expected billings to hold double-digit growth the put skew would not be +7.6 vol points and the stock would not have given back from ~$230 to $190 in the two weeks before the print.
findings.independence: Q2 and Q3 2025 CCB figures are from the company's 8-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1107843/000110784325000037/qlys-20251104xex991.htm); the 7-8% guide itself rests on one secondary summary, so this finding is capped small. Shares the conservative-guide logic with finding 1, but a different line (billings, not revenue).

findings.finding: Vulnerability-management peers that reported after Qualys last spoke: Tenable (2026-10-28) posted Q3 revenue $276.4m, +9.5%, 1.8% above the $271.4m consensus, net expansion up to 107% from 106%, raised its FY, and rose 2.6%; Rapid7 (2026-11-04) beat revenue by 1.6% but its exposure-management ARR fell ~6% and billings fell 5.8%, and the stock still rose 17%. Demand for VM is stable at the leader, weak at the share donor, and the group was paid for beats this season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance measured of QLYS moving on a peer's read-through; QLYS rose with Tenable on a KeyBanc CIO survey (+5.3%) in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Both peers are public and partly priced; QLYS nevertheless fell from ~$225 to $190 after them, so the read-through has not lifted the stock, which argues the peer read is not reflected in it.
findings.independence: Rapid7 Q3 2026 8-K and StockStory recap (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/rpd/news/earnings/rapid7-nasdaqrpd-surprises-with-q3-2026-sales-stock-jumps-17percent), a different company. Proxy, not Qualys's own number.

findings.finding: Short interest is 3.23m shares (~9.3% of 34.6m shares outstanding) with 5.0 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement, roughly unchanged from 3.28m / 4.9 days at 2026-09-30, into a print where the last two beat-and-raises produced +13.8% and +20.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 +20.56% and Q2 2026 +13.78% both came with comparable short interest; Rapid7's +17% this season on a revenue beat with shrinking ARR shows the squeeze mechanism in the peer group.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public but the right tail is what it shapes: the +7.6 put skew says the options market prices the downside more than a squeeze; if the squeeze were priced, calls would be bid over puts.
findings.independence: equibles reported 3.7m / 5.1 days on 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/qlys/short-interest), same FINRA data series.

findings.finding: The stock rose +7.2% intraday on the print day itself (to $204.12 at 12:39 ET from a $190.41 close on 2026-11-06; sealed spot $201.70), after falling from ~$225-231 in late October, so part of any beat is bought before the release and the bar for the reaction is higher.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline run-up 5d -2.84% and 20d +2.5% at seal; no record of a comparable same-day pre-print jump on this name in the cited sources.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself; it bears on how much of the good outcome is left to pay. No news catalyst for the move was found, so it may be anticipation buying.
findings.independence: Fool.com quote box showed $202.48, +6.34% at 1:04 PM ET on 2026-11-09 (https://fool.com/investing/2026/08/05/why-qualys-stock-crushed-it-on-wednesday/). Same price series.

findings.finding: Q3 is the US federal fiscal year-end quarter, and Qualys enters it with TotalCloud newly FedRAMP High authorised (DEA-sponsored, 2026-05-14) and a CEO quote in the Q2 release about 'a growing federal pipeline of new business opportunity'; no specific award was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 prints have been the name's largest up moves (+20.56% in 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: A federal billings contribution is not in any consensus line item; if it were expected, billings estimates would sit above the 7-8% H2 guide.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 8-K CEO quote (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001107843/000110784326000034/qlys-20260804xex991.htm). Inference only; no USAspending award located.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said post-Mythos demand was producing more customer conversations and pilots but most had not yet turned into spending; Q3 is the first quarter in which conversion could show, while Tenable has already integrated Claude Mythos into Tenable One.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Mythos-era AI disruption fear cut the stock >13% in two days in spring 2026; a KeyBanc CIO survey saying Mythos raises cyber budgets lifted it 5.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Pilot conversion has no number attached anywhere; the stock's whipsaw on AI headlines shows the market has no settled view, which is why it is sized small either way.
findings.independence: Valens Research on the Mythos sell-off and rebound (https://www.valens-research.com/investor-essentials-daily/ai-fears-led-investors-undervalue-cybersecurity-firm/). Snippet-level source (MarketBeat page returned 403).

findings.finding: The August FY non-GAAP EPS raise to $7.74-7.88 left the midpoint ($7.81) below the $7.86 consensus of the time, and management expects FY operating expenses to rise in the low teens, which caps margin upside on any revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose +13.78% in August despite the EPS midpoint sitting under consensus; margin has not been the line it traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced; filed because the EPS bar cannot be resolved and opex growth is the counterweight to a revenue beat.
findings.independence: Zacks opex comment via search snippet (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3025511/); different outlet.

findings.finding: The stock (~$202) sits above most published targets: Wedbush downgraded to Neutral with a $175 target in September 2026, the August MarketBeat consensus target was $168.87, and the highest cited targets were Scotiabank $220 and Northland $208; a beat has to move targets, not only meet them.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Wedbush downgrade cost ~7% on the day; after the Q2 beat the stock gave back 5% within ten days (Simply Wall St, 2026-08-15).
findings.why_not_priced: Targets are public; filed as the reaction-function constraint on how much a beat can pay at this price.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to plan sales.
findings.why_not_priced: Routine and small; carries no information about the quarter, hence zero.
findings.independence: SEC Form 4 dated 2026-09-16 shows the same 10b5-1 plan (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001107843/000155824226000024/form4-09162026_120932.xml).

baseline_tension: The positive lean cuts against the +7.62 put skew and a +7% same-day run into the print, and agrees only with the name's own history of large up moves on beat-and-raise quarters; that is why p_up is held at 55 and the scaled number is about half the findings' sum.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (verify the bar): the H2 7-8% billings guide rests on one secondary call summary, so the billings finding was capped from +0.8 to +0.5; the unresolved EPS consensus is stated in `bar`.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): the federal finding has no award behind it, cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 7 (sign against a strong skew): the lean runs against +7.62 vol points of put skew, so p_up moved from 57 to 55, taking the scaled number from +1.4 to +1.0.

Rule 3 (set read): the valuation finding's caveat (targets are public) reduced it from -0.3 to -0.2; the two positioning findings (short interest +, same-day run-up -) can both be true and were kept apart.
Rule 1 left finding 1 at +1.0: this name has paid for beat-and-raise twice in the last four prints, so the reaction function does not veto it.
